• The code lives in its own module so that admin_api.py only asks "does this match?": the rule (length, alphabet, compare) is tested once, and the shells read a file, not a protocol.
• admin_start.py runs before the app exists and before the port is open: no request can reach a half-reset server, and cli.py stays a list of options and banner lines.

• The shells read the file at each welcome instead of making the code themselves: one of several windows may revive the shared server (D445), and each window must still hand over the code that server has now.

• The page keeps the code in sessionStorage (this tab only), never in localStorage or a cookie, and drops it once an administrator exists. Documents, their keys and settings.json are not touched by any of this.
